NASB.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.2: 'When a person sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD, and deceives his companion in regard to a deposit or a security entrusted [to him], or through robbery, or [if] he has extorted from his companion,
NASB.3: or has found what was lost and lied about it and sworn falsely, so that he sins in regard to any one of the things a man may do;
NASB.4: then it shall be, when he sins and becomes guilty, that he shall restore what he took by robbery or what he got by extortion, or the deposit which was entrusted to him or the lost thing which he found,
NASB.5: or anything about which he swore falsely; he shall make restitution for it in full and add to it one-fifth more. He shall give it to the one to whom it belongs on the day [he presents] his guilt offering.
NASB.6: 'Then he shall bring to the priest his guilt offering to the LORD, a ram without defect from the flock, according to your valuation, for a guilt offering,
NASB.7: and the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for any one of the things which he may have done to incur guilt.'
NASB.8: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.9: 'Command Aaron and his sons, saying, 'This is the law for the burnt offering: the burnt offering itself [shall remain] on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning, and the fire on the altar is to be kept burning on it.
NASB.10: 'The priest is to put on his linen robe, and he shall put on undergarments next to his flesh; and he shall take up the ashes [to] which the fire reduces the burnt offering on the altar and place them beside the altar.
NASB.11: 'Then he shall take off his garments and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
NASB.12: 'The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it. It shall not go out, but the priest shall burn wood on it every morning; and he shall lay out the burnt offering on it, and offer up in smoke the fat portions of the peace offerings on it.
NASB.13: 'Fire shall be kept burning continually on the altar; it is not to go out.
NASB.14: 'Now this is the law of the grain offering: the sons of Aaron shall present it before the LORD in front of the altar.
NASB.15: 'Then one [of them] shall lift up from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, with its oil and all the incense that is on the grain offering, and he shall offer [it] up in smoke on the altar, a soothing aroma, as its memorial offering to the LORD.
NASB.16: 'What is left of it Aaron and his sons are to eat. It shall be eaten as unleavened cakes in a holy place; they are to eat it in the court of the tent of meeting.
NASB.17: 'It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their share from My offerings by fire; it is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
NASB.18: 'Every male among the sons of Aaron may eat it; it is a permanent ordinance throughout your generations, from the offerings by fire to the LORD. Whoever touches them will become consecrated.''
NASB.19: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.20: 'This is the offering which Aaron and his sons are to present to the LORD on the day when he is anointed; the tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
NASB.21: 'It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle. When it is [well] stirred, you shall bring it. You shall present the grain offering in baked pieces as a soothing aroma to the LORD.
NASB.22: 'The anointed priest who will be in his place among his sons shall offer it. By a permanent ordinance it shall be entirely offered up in smoke to the LORD.
NASB.23: 'So every grain offering of the priest shall be burned entirely. It shall not be eaten.'
NASB.24: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.25: 'Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, 'This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is slain the sin offering shall be slain before the LORD; it is most holy.
NASB.26: 'The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the tent of meeting.
NASB.27: 'Anyone who touches its flesh will become consecrated; and when any of its blood splashes on a garment, in a holy place you shall wash what was splashed on.
NASB.28: 'Also the earthenware vessel in which it was boiled shall be broken; and if it was boiled in a bronze vessel, then it shall be scoured and rinsed in water.
NASB.29: 'Every male among the priests may eat of it; it is most holy.
NASB.30: 'But no sin offering of which any of the blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place shall be eaten; it shall be burned with fire.

ESV.1: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.2: “If anyone sins and commits a breach of faith against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor in a matter of deposit or security, or through robbery, or if he has oppressed his neighbor
ESV.3: or has found something lost and lied about it, swearing falsely — in any of all the things that people do and sin thereby —
ESV.4: if he has sinned and has realized his guilt and will restore what he took by robbery or what he got by oppression or the deposit that was committed to him or the lost thing that he found
ESV.5: or anything about which he has sworn falsely, he shall restore it in full and shall add a fifth to it, and give it to him to whom it belongs on the day he realizes his guilt.
ESV.6: And he shall bring to the priest as his compensation to the LORD a ram without blemish out of the flock, or its equivalent, for a guilt offering.
ESV.7: And the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he shall be forgiven for any of the things that one may do and thereby become guilty.”
ESV.8: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.9: “Command Aaron and his sons, saying, This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering shall be on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.
ESV.10: And the priest shall put on his linen garment and put his linen undergarment on his body, and he shall take up the ashes to which the fire has reduced the burnt offering on the altar and put them beside the altar.
ESV.11: Then he shall take off his garments and put on other garments and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
ESV.12: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it; it shall not go out. The priest shall burn wood on it every morning, and he shall arrange the burnt offering on it and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.
ESV.13: Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.
ESV.14: “And this is the law of the grain offering. The sons of Aaron shall offer it before the LORD in front of the altar.
ESV.15: And one shall take from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering and its oil and all the frankincense that is on the grain offering and burn this as its memorial portion on the altar, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
ESV.16: And the rest of it Aaron and his sons shall eat. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place. In the court of the tent of meeting they shall eat it.
ESV.17: It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their portion of my food offerings. It is a thing most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
ESV.18: Every male among the children of Aaron may eat of it, as decreed forever throughout your generations, from the LORD's food offerings. Whatever touches them shall become holy.”
ESV.19: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.20: “This is the offering that Aaron and his sons shall offer to the LORD on the day when he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah  of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
ESV.21: It shall be made with oil on a griddle. You shall bring it well mixed, in baked  pieces like a grain offering, and offer it for a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
ESV.22: The priest from among Aaron's sons, who is anointed to succeed him, shall offer it to the LORD as decreed forever. The whole of it shall be burned.
ESV.23: Every grain offering of a priest shall be wholly burned. It shall not be eaten.”
ESV.24: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.25: “Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying, This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where the burnt offering is killed shall the sin offering be killed before the LORD; it is most holy.
ESV.26: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. In a holy place it shall be eaten, in the court of the tent of meeting.
ESV.27: Whatever touches its flesh shall be holy, and when any of its blood is splashed on a garment, you shall wash that on which it was splashed in a holy place.
ESV.28: And the earthenware vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken. But if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, that shall be scoured and rinsed in water.
ESV.29: Every male among the priests may eat of it; it is most holy.
ESV.30: But no sin offering shall be eaten from which any blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place; it shall be burned up with fire.

NKJV.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NKJV.2: “If a person sins and commits a trespass against the LORD by lying to his neighbor about what was delivered to him for safekeeping, or about a pledge, or about a robbery, or if he has extorted from his neighbor,
NKJV.3: or if he has found what was lost and lies concerning it, and swears falsely—in any one of these things that a man may do in which he sins:
NKJV.4: then it shall be, because he has sinned and is guilty, that he shall restore what he has stolen, or the thing which he has extorted, or what was delivered to him for safekeeping, or the lost thing which he found,
NKJV.5: or all that about which he has sworn falsely. He shall restore its full value, add one-fifth more to it, and give it to whomever it belongs, on the day of his trespass offering.
NKJV.6: And he shall bring his trespass offering to the LORD, a ram without blemish from the flock, with your valuation, as a trespass offering, to the priest.
NKJV.7: So the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he shall be forgiven for any one of these things that he may have done in which he trespasses.”
NKJV.8: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NKJV.9: “Command Aaron and his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the burnt offering: The burnt offering shall be on the hearth upon the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.
NKJV.10: And the priest shall put on his linen garment, and his linen trousers he shall put on his body, and take up the ashes of the burnt offering which the fire has consumed on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
NKJV.11: Then he shall take off his garments, put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
NKJV.12: And the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it; it shall not be put out. And the priest shall burn wood on it every morning, and lay the burnt offering in order on it; and he shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.
NKJV.13: A fire shall always be burning on the altar; it shall never go out.
NKJV.14: ‘This is the law of the grain offering: The sons of Aaron shall offer it on the altar before the LORD.
NKJV.15: He shall take from it his handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, with its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the grain offering, and shall burn it on the altar for a sweet aroma, as a memorial to the LORD.
NKJV.16: And the remainder of it Aaron and his sons shall eat; with unleavened bread it shall be eaten in a holy place; in the court of the tabernacle of meeting they shall eat it.
NKJV.17: It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their portion of My offerings made by fire; it is most holy, like the sin offering and the trespass offering.
NKJV.18: All the males among the children of Aaron may eat it. It shall be a statute forever in your generations concerning the offerings made by fire to the LORD. Everyone who touches them must be holy.’ ”
NKJV.19: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NKJV.20: “This is the offering of Aaron and his sons, which they shall offer to the LORD, beginning on the day when he is anointed: one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a daily grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it at night.
NKJV.21: It shall be made in a pan with oil. When it is mixed, you shall bring it in. The baked pieces of the grain offering you shall offer for a sweet aroma to the LORD.
NKJV.22: The priest from among his sons, who is anointed in his place, shall offer it. It is a statute forever to the LORD. It shall be wholly burned.
NKJV.23: For every grain offering for the priest shall be wholly burned. It shall not be eaten.”
NKJV.24: Also the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NKJV.25: “Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is killed, the sin offering shall be killed before the LORD. It is most holy.
NKJV.26: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. In a holy place it shall be eaten, in the court of the tabernacle of meeting.
NKJV.27: Everyone who touches its flesh must be holy. And when its blood is sprinkled on any garment, you shall wash that on which it was sprinkled, in a holy place.
NKJV.28: But the earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken. And if it is boiled in a bronze pot, it shall be both scoured and rinsed in water.
NKJV.29: All the males among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
NKJV.30: But no sin offering from which any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle of meeting, to make atonement in the holy place, shall be eaten. It shall be burned in the fire.

CSB17.2: “When someone sins and offends the LORD by deceiving <sup>ⓜ</sup> his neighbor in regard to a deposit, <sup>ⓝ</sup> a security, <sup>[1]</sup> or a robbery; <sup>ⓐ</sup> or defrauds <sup>ⓑ</sup> his neighbor;
CSB17.3: or finds something lost and lies about it; <sup>ⓒ</sup> or swears falsely <sup>ⓓ</sup> about any of the sinful things a person may do —
CSB17.4: once he has sinned <sup>ⓔ</sup> and acknowledged his guilt <sup>ⓕ</sup>  — he must return what he stole or defrauded, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost item he found,
CSB17.5: or anything else about which he swore falsely. He will make full restitution for it and add a fifth of its value to it. <sup>ⓖ</sup> He is to pay it to its owner on the day he acknowledges his guilt. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.6: Then he is to bring his guilt offering <sup>ⓘ</sup> to the LORD: an unblemished <sup>ⓙ</sup> ram from the flock according to your assessment of its value as a guilt offering to the priest.
CSB17.7: In this way the priest will make atonement on his behalf before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for anything he may have done to incur guilt.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.9: “Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the burnt offering; the burnt offering itself must remain on the altar’s hearth all night until morning, while the fire of the altar is kept burning on it.
CSB17.10: The priest is to put on his linen robe and linen undergarments. <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup> He is to remove the ashes of the burnt offering the fire has consumed on the altar, and place them beside the altar.
CSB17.11: Then he will take off his garments, put on other clothes, <sup>ⓜ</sup> and bring the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.
CSB17.12: The fire on the altar is to be kept burning; it must not go out. Every morning the priest will burn wood on the fire. He is to arrange the burnt offering on the fire and burn the fat portions from the fellowship offerings <sup>ⓝ</sup> on it.
CSB17.13: Fire must be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not go out.
CSB17.14: “Now this is the law of the grain offering: <sup>ⓐ</sup> Aaron’s sons will present it before the LORD in front of the altar.
CSB17.15: The priest is to remove a handful of fine flour and olive oil from the grain offering, with all the frankincense that is on the offering, and burn its memorial portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
CSB17.16: Aaron and his sons may eat the rest of it. <sup>ⓑ</sup> It is to be eaten in the form of unleavened bread <sup>ⓒ</sup> in a holy place; <sup>ⓓ</sup> they are to eat it in the courtyard <sup>ⓔ</sup> of the tent of meeting.
CSB17.17: It must not be baked with yeast; I have assigned it as their portion <sup>ⓕ</sup> from my fire offerings. <sup>ⓖ</sup> It is especially holy, like the sin offering <sup>ⓗ</sup> and the guilt offering.
CSB17.18: Any male among Aaron’s descendants <sup>ⓘ</sup> may eat it. It is a permanent portion <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓙ</sup> throughout your generations from the fire offerings to the LORD. Anything that touches the offerings will become holy.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.20: “This is the offering that Aaron and his sons are to present to the LORD on the day that he is anointed: two quarts <sup>[4]</sup> of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
CSB17.21: It is to be prepared with oil on a griddle; you are to bring it well-kneaded. You are to present it as a grain offering of baked pieces, <sup>[5]</sup> a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
CSB17.22: The priest, who is one of Aaron’s sons and will be anointed to take his place, is to prepare it. It must be completely burned as a permanent portion for the LORD.
CSB17.23: Every grain offering for a priest will be a whole burnt offering; <sup>ⓛ</sup> it is not to be eaten.”
CSB17.25: “Tell Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the sin offering. <sup>ⓜ</sup> The sin offering is most holy and must be slaughtered before the LORD at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
CSB17.26: The priest who offers it as a sin offering will eat it. It is to be eaten in a holy place, <sup>ⓝ</sup> in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
CSB17.27: Anything that touches its flesh will become holy, and if any of its blood spatters on a garment, then you must wash that garment <sup>[6]</sup> in a holy place.
CSB17.28: A clay pot in which the sin offering is boiled is to be broken; if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it is to be scoured and rinsed with water.
CSB17.29: Any male among the priests may eat it; it is especially holy.
CSB17.30: But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood has been brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place; it must be burned.

WEB.2: “If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against Yahweh, and deals falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,
WEB.3: or has found that which was lost, and dealt falsely therein, and swearing to a lie; in any of these things that a man does, sinning therein;
WEB.4: then it shall be, if he has sinned, and is guilty, he shall restore that which he took by robbery, or the thing which he has gotten by oppression, or the deposit which was committed to him, or the lost thing which he found,
WEB.5: or any thing about which he has sworn falsely; he shall restore it even in full, and shall add a fifth part more to it. To him to whom it belongs he shall give it, in the day of his being found guilty.
WEB.6: He shall bring his trespass offering to Yahweh, a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest.
WEB.7: The priest shall make atonement for him before Yahweh, and he will be forgiven concerning whatever he does to become guilty.”
WEB.9: “Command Aaron and his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the burnt offering: the burnt offering shall be on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning; and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.
WEB.10: The priest shall put on his linen garment, and he shall put on his linen breeches upon his body; and he shall remove the ashes from where the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
WEB.11: He shall take off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
WEB.12: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it, it shall not go out; and the priest shall burn wood on it every morning: and he shall lay the burnt offering in order upon it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.
WEB.13: Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.
WEB.14: “‘This is the law of the meal offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before Yahweh, before the altar.
WEB.15: He shall take from there his handful of the fine flour of the meal offering, and of its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the meal offering, and shall burn it on the altar for a pleasant aroma, as its memorial, to Yahweh.
WEB.16: That which is left of it Aaron and his sons shall eat. It shall be eaten without yeast in a holy place. They shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
WEB.17: It shall not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their portion of my offerings made by fire. It is most holy, as the sin offering, and as the trespass offering.
WEB.18: Every male among the children of Aaron shall eat of it, as their portion forever throughout your generations, from the offerings of Yahweh made by fire. Whoever touches them shall be holy.’”
WEB.20: “This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons, which they shall offer to Yahweh in the day when he is anointed: one tenth of an ephah  of fine flour for a meal offering perpetually, half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening.
WEB.21: It shall be made with oil in a griddle. When it is soaked, you shall bring it in. You shall offer the meal offering in baked pieces for a pleasant aroma to Yahweh.
WEB.22: The anointed priest that will be in his place from among his sons shall offer it. By a statute forever, it shall be wholly burned to Yahweh.
WEB.23: Every meal offering of a priest shall be wholly burned. It shall not be eaten.”
WEB.25: “Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is killed, the sin offering shall be killed before Yahweh. It is most holy.
WEB.26: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
WEB.27: Whatever shall touch its flesh shall be holy. When there is any of its blood sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash that on which it was sprinkled in a holy place.
WEB.28: But the earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured, and rinsed in water.
WEB.29: Every male among the priests shall eat of it: it is most holy.
WEB.30: No sin offering, of which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, shall be eaten: it shall be burned with fire.

NLT.1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.2: “Suppose one of you sins against your associate and is unfaithful to the LORD. Suppose you cheat in a deal involving a security deposit, or you steal or commit fraud,
NLT.3: or you find lost property and lie about it, or you lie while swearing to tell the truth, or you commit any other such sin.
NLT.4: If you have sinned in any of these ways, you are guilty. You must give back whatever you stole, or the money you took by extortion, or the security deposit, or the lost property you found,
NLT.5: or anything obtained by swearing falsely. You must make restitution by paying the full price plus an additional 20 percent to the person you have harmed. On the same day you must present a guilt offering.
NLT.6: As a guilt offering to the LORD, you must bring to the priest your own ram with no defects, or you may buy one of equal value.
NLT.7: Through this process, the priest will purify you before the LORD, making you right with him, and you will be forgiven for any of these sins you have committed.”
NLT.8: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.9: “Give Aaron and his sons the following instructions regarding the burnt offering. The burnt offering must be left on top of the altar until the next morning, and the fire on the altar must be kept burning all night.
NLT.10: In the morning, after the priest on duty has put on his official linen clothing and linen undergarments, he must clean out the ashes of the burnt offering and put them beside the altar.
NLT.11: Then he must take off these garments, change back into his regular clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a place that is ceremonially clean.
NLT.12: Meanwhile, the fire on the altar must be kept burning; it must never go out. Each morning the priest will add fresh wood to the fire and arrange the burnt offering on it. He will then burn the fat of the peace offerings on it.
NLT.13: Remember, the fire must be kept burning on the altar at all times. It must never go out.
NLT.14: “These are the instructions regarding the grain offering. Aaron’s sons must present this offering to the LORD in front of the altar.
NLT.15: The priest on duty will take from the grain offering a handful of the choice flour moistened with olive oil, together with all the frankincense. He will burn this representative portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
NLT.16: Aaron and his sons may eat the rest of the flour, but it must be baked without yeast and eaten in a sacred place within the courtyard of the Tabernacle.
NLT.17: Remember, it must never be prepared with yeast. I have given it to the priests as their share of the special gifts presented to me. Like the sin offering and the guilt offering, it is most holy.
NLT.18: Any of Aaron’s male descendants may eat from the special gifts presented to the LORD. This is their permanent right from generation to generation. Anyone or anything that touches these offerings will become holy.”
NLT.19: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.20: “On the day Aaron and his sons are anointed, they must present to the LORD the standard grain offering of two quarts of choice flour, half to be offered in the morning and half to be offered in the evening.
NLT.21: It must be carefully mixed with olive oil and cooked on a griddle. Then slice this grain offering and present it as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
NLT.22: In each generation, the high priest who succeeds Aaron must prepare this same offering. It belongs to the LORD and must be burned up completely. This is a permanent law.
NLT.23: All such grain offerings of a priest must be burned up entirely. None of it may be eaten.”
NLT.24: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.25: “Give Aaron and his sons the following instructions regarding the sin offering. The animal given as an offering for sin is a most holy offering, and it must be slaughtered in the LORD’s presence at the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.
NLT.26: The priest who offers the sacrifice as a sin offering must eat his portion in a sacred place within the courtyard of the Tabernacle.
NLT.27: Anyone or anything that touches the sacrificial meat will become holy. If any of the sacrificial blood spatters on a person’s clothing, the soiled garment must be washed in a sacred place.
NLT.28: If a clay pot is used to boil the sacrificial meat, it must then be broken. If a bronze pot is used, it must be scoured and thoroughly rinsed with water.
NLT.29: Any male from a priest’s family may eat from this offering; it is most holy.
NLT.30: But the offering for sin may not be eaten if its blood was brought into the Tabernacle as an offering for purification in the Holy Place. It must be completely burned with fire.

AMP.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.2: "When anyone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor (companion, associate) in regard to a deposit or a security entrusted to him, or through robbery, or if he has extorted from his neighbor,
AMP.3: or has found what was lost and lied about it and sworn falsely, so that he sins in regard to any one of the things a man may do—
AMP.4: then if he has sinned and is guilty, he shall restore what he took by robbery, or what he got by extortion, or the deposit which was entrusted to him, or the lost thing which he found,
AMP.5: or anything about which he has sworn falsely; he shall not only restore it in full, but shall add to it one-fifth more. He shall give it to the one to whom it belongs on the day of his guilt offering.
AMP.6: Then he shall bring to the priest his guilt offering to the LORD, a ram without blemish from the flock, as valued by you, as a guilt offering.
AMP.7: The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for any one of the things which he may have done to incur guilt."
AMP.8: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.9: "Command Aaron and his sons, saying, 'This is the law of the burnt offering: the burnt offering shall remain on the hearth that is on the altar all night until morning and the fire is to be kept burning on the altar.
AMP.10: The priest is to put on his linen robe, with his linen undergarments next to his body. Then he shall take up the ashes of the burnt offering which the fire has consumed on the altar and put them beside the altar.
AMP.11: Then he shall take off his garments and put on something else, and take the ashes outside the camp to a (ceremonially) clean place.
AMP.12: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it shall not [be allowed to] go out. The priest shall burn wood on it every morning, and he shall arrange the burnt offering on it and offer the fat portions of the peace offerings up in smoke on it.
AMP.13: The fire shall be burning continually on the altar; it shall not [be allowed to] go out.
AMP.14: 'Now this is the law of the grain offering: the sons of Aaron shall present it before the LORD in front of the altar.
AMP.15: One of them shall take up from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering with its oil and all the incense that is on the grain offering, and he shall offer it up in smoke on the altar, a sweet and soothing aroma, as the memorial offering to the LORD.
AMP.16: What is left of it Aaron and his sons are to eat. It shall be eaten as unleavened bread in a holy place; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
AMP.17: It shall not be baked with leaven [which represents corruption or sin]. I have given it as their share of My offerings by fire; it is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
AMP.18: Every male among the sons of Aaron may eat it [as his share]; it is a permanent ordinance throughout your generations, from offerings by fire to the LORD. Whatever touches them will become consecrated (ceremonially clean).'"
AMP.19: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.20: "This is the offering which Aaron and his sons are to present to the LORD on the day when he is anointed: the tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
AMP.21: It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle. When it is well stirred, you shall bring it. You shall present the grain offering in baked pieces as a sweet and soothing aroma to the LORD.
AMP.22: The priest from among the sons of Aaron who is anointed in his place shall offer it. By a permanent statute it shall be entirely offered up in smoke to the LORD.
AMP.23: So every grain offering of the priest shall be burned entirely. It shall not be eaten."
AMP.24: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.25: "Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying, 'This is the law of the sin offering: the sin offering shall be killed before the LORD in the [same] place where the burnt offering is killed; it is most holy.
AMP.26: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
AMP.27: Whatever touches its meat will become consecrated (ceremonially clean). When any of its blood splashes on a garment, you shall wash what was splashed on in a holy place.
AMP.28: Also the earthenware vessel in which it was boiled shall be broken; and if it was boiled in a bronze vessel, then that vessel shall be scoured and rinsed in water.
AMP.29: Every male among the priests may eat this offering; it is most holy.
AMP.30: But no sin offering from which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place shall be eaten; it shall be [completely] burned in the fire.

MSG.2: "When anyone sins by betraying trust with God by deceiving his neighbor regarding something entrusted to him, or by robbing or cheating or threatening him;
MSG.3: or if he has found something lost and lies about it and swears falsely regarding any of these sins that people commonly commit—

NET.10: Then the priest must put on his linen robe and must put linen leggings over his bare flesh, and he must take up the fatty ashes of the burnt offering that the fire consumed on the altar, and he must place them beside the altar.
NET.11: Then he must take off his clothes and put on other clothes, and he must bring the fatty ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place,
NET.12: but the fire which is on the altar must be kept burning on it. It must not be extinguished. So the priest must kindle wood on it morning by morning, and he must arrange the burnt offering on it and offer the fat of the peace offering up in smoke on it.
NET.13: A continual fire must be kept burning on the altar. It must not be extinguished.
NET.14: “‘This is the law of the grain offering. The sons of Aaron are to present it before the LORD in front of the altar,
NET.15: and the priest must take up with his hand some of the choice wheat flour of the grain offering and some of its olive oil, and all of the frankincense that is on the grain offering, and he must offer its memorial portion up in smoke on the altar as a soothing aroma to the LORD.
NET.16: Aaron and his sons are to eat what is left over from it. It must be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the Meeting Tent.
NET.17: It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their portion from my gifts. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
NET.18: Every male among the sons of Aaron may eat it. It is a perpetual allotted portion throughout your generations from the gifts of the LORD. Anyone who touches these gifts must be holy.’”
NET.19: Then the LORD spoke to Moses:
NET.20: “This is the offering of Aaron and his sons which they must present to the LORD on the day when he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of choice wheat flour as a continual grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
NET.21: It must be made with olive oil on a griddle and you must bring it well soaked, so you must present a grain offering of broken pieces as a soothing aroma to the LORD.
NET.22: The high priest who succeeds him from among his sons must do it. It is a perpetual statute; it must be offered up in smoke as a whole offering to the LORD.
NET.23: Every grain offering of a priest must be a whole offering; it must not be eaten.”
NET.24: Then the LORD spoke to Moses:
NET.25: “Tell Aaron and his sons, ‘This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered the sin offering must be slaughtered before the LORD. It is most holy.
NET.26: The priest who offers it for sin is to eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Meeting Tent.
NET.27: Anyone who touches its meat must be holy, and whoever spatters some of its blood on a garment, you must wash whatever he spatters it on in a holy place.
NET.28: Any clay vessel it is boiled in must be broken, and if it was boiled in a bronze vessel, then that vessel must be rubbed out and rinsed in water.
NET.29: Any male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
NET.30: But any sin offering from which some of its blood is brought into the Meeting Tent to make atonement in the sanctuary must not be eaten. It must be burned up in the fire.
